newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Conglomerates drive Nigerian stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Conglomerates drive Nigerian stocks higher.

text.p: Nigeria's top conglomerates were the toast of trading on the Nigerian Stock Exchange on Tuesday, driving an already buoyant market further up.
The all-share index rose to 8,210.43 from Monday's 8137.14 close as activity in the multinationals entered a higher gear, traders said.
"The conglomerates were on the bullish side in anticipation of better results," trader Chuks Ohanwunsi of Networth Securities, said.
Investors with plenty of cash therefore helped the stocks to close with impressive price gains, he said.
PZ Industries, the sector's leader, was up 45 kobo at 25.25 naira while Lever Brothers and UAC closed respectively at 24.10 naira and 13.60 naira, up 40 kobo each.
Food, bank as well as oil marketing shares kept attracting buyers despite their high prices, dealers said.
Nigerian Bottling Company, the local Coca-Cola bottlers, rose 35 kobo to 48.85 naira. Nestle was 65.30 naira and Cadbury closed at 36.20 naira, both moving 30 kobo up.
Hopes of capital appreciation was equally responsible for the rise of bank shares. Afribank up 35 kobo at 7.85 naira, was the biggest beneficiary, dealers said.
First Bank, at 16.80 naira, Union Bank at 14.50 naira and UBA at 12.40 naira were respective 20 kobo gainers.
Industrial Gases ended at 8.00 naira, 20 kobo higher on an improved first quarter result to end-December 1996.
Continuous scrambling for oil marketers saw Total add 39 kobo to 72.99 naira. Mobil too finished 35 kobo up at 63.40 naira while Unipetrol rose 30 kobo to 75.80 naira.
But textile companies slumped on their worsening outlook, traders said.
Worst hit was Afprint which lost five kobo at 2.19 naira. Aba Textiles dropped one kobo to 3.55 naira.
Benue Cement Company, trying to find a stable price, fell six kobo to finish at 5.60 naira.
